payload.data: March 1938. Japan's armies drive down the Tianjin–Pukou railway toward Xuzhou. In the way, round Tengxian, stand the Sichuan troops of Sun Zhen's 22nd Group Army: tired men, a third of them with no rifle, only grenades.
04:00, 14 March: the Seya Detachment, a brigade of Isogai's 10th Division, attacks in three columns: the 10th Infantry on the right, the guns down the railway, the 63rd Infantry on the left.
11:00: the 63rd takes Xiangcheng, headquarters of the 125th Division.
On the right the 10th breaks the 370th Brigade at Shiqiang. At 19:00 the brigade falls back on Dawu, west of Tengxian.
18:10: the 63rd enters Jiehe village, astride the railway. The Chinese line from Jiehe to Longshan holds on into the next day.
10:30, 15 March, at Jiehe: Seya does not go straight down the railway. He sends the detachment round the east of Tengxian, by Dongguo and Wangmiao, to attack the city from the east.
The Japanese records route the swing far to the east, by Dongguo and Wangmiao; Chinese accounts have its van at Longyangdian, north-east of the city.
At Chengtou the Japanese light armour scatters Wang Wenzhen's 731st Regiment.
damaged
Wang Mingzhang is ordered to hold Tengxian three days for Tang Enbo's corps. He has one regiment and no heavy weapons. Sun Zhen: "That is my order; if it is not held, that is on you."
Yan Yi's battalion reaches the city at 17:00 and takes the east suburb; Zhang Xuanwu's 727th Regiment comes in at dusk, and Zhang takes command of the walls.
The 41st Army's Special Service Battalion arrives by train from Lincheng and holds the south wall. About 2,500 men are in the city; fewer than 2,000 are fighting troops.
Dawn, 16 March. Patrols report the city lightly held, so the 10th Regiment attacks with just five companies. From Xiacun its commander sees a Nazi flag over the German mission inside the walls.
Japanese records are usually in Tokyo time, but this regiment's sunrise and dusk fit local time; the replay reads its times as local.
10:20: eight field guns go into position at Xiacun, 2 km south-east of the walls. Their reach covers the city many times over.
11:00: a Chinese armoured train with 75 mm guns runs south from the station, firing; the field guns duel with it for ten minutes.
11:15: the heavy battalion ranges on the east suburb's gate. Its first round hits.
Whether the heavy battalion's twelve guns were 15 cm or 10.5 cm howitzers is disputed; the replay draws the 15 cm Type 4's 8.8 km range.
Noon: the 3rd Company's assault stops 50 m short of the suburb wall. The guns are told to make a breach first.
No Chinese 15 cm howitzer fired at Tengxian: the 10th Artillery's sFH 18/32L came with Tang Enbo's corps and first fired at Taierzhuang, on 27 or 28 March.
destroyed
14:15: through the breach the 3rd Company takes a corner of the east suburb. Grenades keep it there.
Chinese accounts have the Japanese who broke into the east suburb thrown out at dusk; the Japanese report has them holding a corner of it all night.
18:40, under a full moon: the 3rd Battalion breaks into the south suburb.
21:00: Wang gives up the outer positions. At midnight the remnants of the 370th and 372nd Brigades come in by the west gate.

07:30, 17 March: the guns open again, now with the China Garrison's modern Type 96 15 cm howitzers. At 08:30 breaching fire begins: 40 m south of the east gate, and 20 m west of the south-east corner.
damaged
Fifty rounds nearly make the east breach. The city burns, and a south wind blows the smoke north over the defenders.
10:00: a Japanese observer fights his way up the Longquan pagoda, 30 m above the city, and directs the guns.
Noon: Wang's last telegram to Sun Zhen: resolved "to fight to the death, to repay the nation and your trust".
13:00: Colonel Akashiba is grazed by a sniper. He stays in command.
14:30: the 10th's 2nd Battalion arrives and is sent to the station, to shut the way out west.
The 3rd Battalion's assault on the south breach is thrown back by grenades. At 16:05 it is on the wall, and fights west along it.
damaged
damaged
The west gate falls at about 17:00. Wang and his staff are let down from the north-west corner, to reach the troops at the station.
destroyed
destroyed
In the moat outside the west gate, machine guns on the gate tower cut down Wang Mingzhang, his chief of staff Zhao Weibin and some ten others.
Accounts of Wang Mingzhang's death differ in time and place; most put it at dusk in the moat outside the west gate, under fire from the gate tower.
damaged
Five or six hundred men who get out westward are caught at the station by the 2nd Battalion. Outside the north gate the 124th Division's chief of staff, Zou Shaomeng, is shot.
21:00: some two hundred men of the 727th open the walled-up north gate and break out.
destroyed
destroyed
21:40: the 1st Battalion is over the east wall. By 23:00 it holds the north gate.
destroyed
destroyed
18 March: the city is cleared house by house; by 14:00 it is over. Li Zongren later: without Tengxian's hard defence there would have been no victory at Taierzhuang.
